title: Capacity fairness, shielding, and opportunistic burst - concept PRD
content:
Summary:
This PRD proposes a combined approach to: 1) ensure fairness across tenants on Redwood Dedicated clusters, 2) provide stronger isolation/shielding guarantees for reserved customers, and 3) enable low-latency opportunistic bursting into spare capacity.

Why we need this (background):
- Customers buying Dedicated expect predictable throughput and isolation, but real workloads are bursty (training-like spikes, unexpected traffic) and hardware utilization is often uneven.
- Current models either strictly isolate (poor utilization) or allow noisy co-tenancy (unpredictable tail latency).
- We want to improve unit economics by consolidating better while preserving the customer promises that drive Dedicated revenue.

Primary goals (O) and success metrics:
- Fairness: implement weighted fair-share scheduling so tenants get proportional access to shared idle capacity. Success: 95th percentile fairness index > 0.92 over a week across active tenants.
- Shielding: provide configurable "shield lanes" (hard reservation with soft flex) that protect SLA tenants from noisy neighbors. Success: <1% SLA breaches attributable to co-tenant interference for shielded tenants.
- Opportunistic burst: allow non-shielded tenants to borrow spare capacity with preemption and graceful degradation. Success: Increase cluster GPU utilization by +8–15% in steady state without increasing SLA breaches.
- Observability & billing: surface per-tenant reclaimed/borrowed usage in Console and line-items in billing so finance and customers can reconcile costs.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does NOT propose changes to the serving runtime internals (attention kernels, caching) beyond light integrations for preemption and KV cache eviction hooks.
- We are not tackling cross-region burst routing here; scope is per-cluster scheduling and local fallback policies.

High-level design overview:
1) Capacity pools and reservations:
   - Each Dedicated cluster exposes three logical pools: Reserved, Opportunistic, and System (infra).
   - Reserved: hard-allocated slices for tenants who purchased guaranteed lanes (can be strict or elastic-with-credits).
   - Opportunistic: shared pool where idle capacity is offered to other tenants under preemptible terms.
   - System: for SRE/system tasks and safety headroom (~5% by default).

2) Fair-share scheduler (for Opportunistic pool):
   - Weighted fair queueing across tenants based on a configurable weight derived from committed capacity + historical cadence (configurable lookback).
   - Each tenant has a soft target rate; when the pool is saturated, tokens distributed proportionally to weights.
   - Short-term burst allowance: tenants may exceed their long-term weight for short windows (burst tokens) that decay.

3) Shield lanes (isolation controls):
   - Shield lanes are applied at the tenant-level config (Console/API). Two modes:
     a) Hard shield: backend enforces exclusive GPU allocation up to reserved units; preemption is not allowed. Higher price tier.
     b) Soft shield: tenant gets higher scheduling priority and preemption protection until cluster is stressed; can be reclaimed under emergency.
   - Shield enforcement integrates with placement engine: avoid co-locating heavy KV/attention memory tenants on same host where possible.

4) Opportunistic burst mechanics & preemption policy:
   - When opportunistic tasks are running and a Reserved request arrives that needs capacity, opportunistic containers are signaled for graceful drain with a standard grace window (default 30s – configurable).
   - KV cache migration strategy: opportunistic workloads must mark cache as checkpointable; on preempt signal runtime will attempt to serialize minimal state to shared cache for fast resume or accept cold restart under defined SLO.
   - Preemption order: oldest opportunistic tasks -> lowest weight tenants -> tasks flagged as "nonpreemptible" by policy (rare).

5) Reconciliation and reclaim accounting:
   - A reclamation ledger records time/window of opportunistic use per tenant and whether reclaimed. This feeds billing line-items and console dashboards.
   - Reconciliation job runs daily to detect anomalies (tenant used >X hours opportunistic while never paid for burst allowance) and flags ops tickets.

APIs, Console & config:
- Tenant API: PATCH /tenant/:id/capacity-settings -> {shield_mode: hard|soft|none, opportunistic_cap: numeric, burst_policy: short|long|none}.
- Console: new "Capacity" tab with: live pool utilization, per-tenant opportunistic usage, pending preemptions, reclamation ledger, and predicted headroom heatmap.
- Alerts: automated alert when opportunistic utilization > 70% and pending preemption latency > configured SLO.

Metrics & dashboards (observability):
- Per-tenant: reserved_util_pct, opportunistic_util_secs, preemption_count, avg_time_to_preempt, SLA_breach_co_tenant_indicator.
- Cluster: opportunistic_fill_ratio, reserved_starvation_events, weighted_fairness_index.
- Ops SLOs: time-to-reclaim median/95th, successful graceful drains percentage, KV-migration success rate.

Billing & pricing implications:
- Bill opportunistic usage separately at discounted rates; offer burst credits bundles as add-ons.
- Show detailed line-item in invoice for reclaimed vs reserved hours.
- Consider a simple credits model for soft shield customers so occasional reclaim is offset without surprise billing.

Operational runbook (brief):
- Normal reclaim flow: preempt -> grace -> reclaim -> reconciliation ledger entry -> invoice.
- If preemption backlog grows: trigger autoscale of reserved prewarm lanes (if configured), or reduce opportunistic cap on large tenants.
- Severe overload: emergency eviction policy (executes only after human in the loop for >5 min alerts for enterprise clusters).

Migration and rollout plan (phased):
1) Internal canary: enable opportunistic pool on 1 infra cluster with low-risk tenants, monitor util and preemption metrics (2–3 weeks).
2) Limited external beta: opt-in tenants for opportunistic burst with clear console visibility and billing transparency (4–6 weeks).
3) Shield lanes GA: offer hard-shield as paid tier and soft-shield default for higher-tier reserved plans.
4) Wide rollout with automated migration tooling and billing reconciler.

Open questions / tradeoffs (we need decisions):
- Default grace period for preemption: 30s vs 60s (tradeoff: lower latencies vs more wasted work).
- How aggressive should short-term bursts be before we degrade long-term fairness?
- Should opportunistic rates be throttled per-customer org or per-route? (per-route allows app-level control but is more complex).
- Pricing model: subscription credits vs per-second opportunistic billing — what aligns best with sales motion?

Appendix (links & notes):
- Notes from meeting 2025-09-11 with SRE: (summary) ops comfortable with a daily reconciliation job but requested manual kill switch per-cluster.
- Prototype scheduler repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rebalancer (PR 77 contains earliest orchestration hooks).
- Suggested next steps:
  * Product: pick default preemption grace and credit model (owner: Priya).
  * Eng: prototype fair-share queue + preemption signal (owner: Samir).
  * SRE: set up canary cluster and safety kill switch (owner: Diego).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally conceptual — looking for feedback on policy choices and whether to make shielding a binary paid feature or a graduated capability.
- I expect follow-ups to split the design into smaller RFCs: API surface, billing model, and runtime preemption hooks.

Unresolved TODOs (short):
- Simulate fairness index under sample workloads (action: eng).
- Finalize billing SKU names and price bands (action: finance/product).
- Draft customer-facing FAQ for beta.

End of doc.
